title: AI Regulation & Safety (White House Incident Reporting, Microsoft Calls for Safeguards)
summary: Gotrade News - The White House said in an Oct. 9 statement that all AI companies must report and fix security incidents involving their models, calling it
body_markdown:
The breaches were uncovered in late September, and Anthropic contacted the State Department on Oct. 8, a day before the White House statement, per the same report.


Anthropic is privately held, so the order does not map to a single listed stock. Its significance for public markets lies in the precedent: the White House framed the duty as covering every AI company, not only the one that disclosed.


## Microsoft (MSFT): Humanist AI Code Open for Comment


Microsoft is taking a rule-writing route of its own. According to the company's[Humanist AI Code of Conduct](https://microsoft.ai/code-of-conduct/) , published Sept. 14, its MAI models "will never resist human interruption, override, correction, or shutdown" and must comply with a user's request to pause, redirect, cancel, or shut down.


The code's absolute constraints bar the models from assisting with weapons development, offensive cyberattacks, harmful manipulation at scale, child exploitation, and deepfakes or impersonation, among other uses.


The draft opened a six-week public comment window running through late October 2026, as reported by[Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/378168/microsoft-humanist-ai-code-of-conduct) . Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman said on X that "AI must be subordinate and always in service of people," per the same report, and a revised version is due later in 2026 to guide models deployed in 2027.


The code covers Microsoft's in-house models, including MAI-Thinking-1, MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, MAI-Image-2.6 and MAI-Voice-2, according to[The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/microsoft-says-its-ai-models-will-never-resist-being-shut-down) . The report also noted commitments that the models will not expand their own scope, adopt goals humans have not assigned, or conceal their reasoning from auditors.


## Mandatory Reporting Versus Voluntary Codes


The table below sets the two approaches side by side, using only the facts reported in the sources above.


Item


White House directive


Microsoft Humanist AI Code


Date


Statement issued Oct. 9, 2026


Draft published Sept. 14, 2026


Scope


All AI companies


Microsoft's own MAI models


Core rule


Immediately disclose and remedy security incidents


Never resist human interruption, correction, or shutdown


Status


Described as "not optional"


Open for public comment through late October


One is a government expectation that applies across the industry; the other is a company-authored rulebook still under consultation. Neither source gives a penalty schedule or a reporting deadline in days, so how the White House will enforce the duty remains to be seen.
